findings.title: Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
findings.body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the deleteMany OR second branch filters only on retryCount gt 1 with no method filter, while the first branch correctly filters method SMS. This deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) that ever have retryCount > 1, not just failed SMS reminders, causing unintended data loss. Fix by adding method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the retryCount branch.

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries
findings.body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the failure paths do data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } based on the value read earlier instead of an atomic increment. If two cron invocations process the same reminder concurrently, one increment is lost, so the reminder can be retried indefinitely and never reach the gt 1 delete threshold, or exceed the intended 2-attempt limit. Use atomic increment operation instead.

findings.title: Missing sendTo/message never counts toward retry limit
findings.body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the guard if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo) does nothing when message is empty or sendTo is falsy: it neither schedules nor increments retryCount. That reminder stays scheduled:false with unchanged retryCount and will be returned by findMany on every cron tick until scheduledDate expires, defeating the PR goal of deleting persistently failing reminders after 2 tries and wasting cron work.
